references.text: Abram leaves his country, his people and his father's household to follow God's call, similar to how the disciples leave everything to follow Jesus.
Jesus calls the first disciples, who leave their nets and follow him, paralleling Peter's statement about having left everything.
Jesus discusses the cost of discipleship, which includes leaving everything to follow him.
Jesus teaches about denying oneself and taking up one's cross to follow him, reflecting the sacrifice of the disciples.
After a miraculous catch of fish, Peter and his partners leave everything and follow Jesus, mirroring Peter's statement in Matthew 19:27.
Peter tells Jesus that they have left everything and followed him, and Jesus responds with the promise of reward, paralleling Matthew 19:27.
Abraham leaves his country in faith, not knowing where he was going, as an example of faith that requires leaving the known for the unknown.
